entries.subject: DLR Dawn HAMO natural color
entries.finding: The retained HAMO natural-color label was inspected: 26704×13080 samples, three byte bands, planetocentric simple-cylindrical mapping, east-positive longitude and center longitude 180°. Its 255 km projection sphere is not the mesh’s measured physical radius. The selected publisher color remains photometrically corrected 650/550/430 nm imagery with its recorded clipping and registration limitations; no new browser qualification was performed by reading the label.

entries.subject: DLR HAMO corrected monochrome
entries.finding: DLR HAMO corrected monochrome — Complementary candidate, excluded from this selection: natural color supplies the same broad surface interpretation; a separate grayscale view would duplicate it.
entries.revisitWhen: A changed source release adds independently useful geometry or metadata beyond the selected model; compare it before changing the displayed source.

entries.subject: DLR HAMO Clementine ratios
entries.finding: [DLR HAMO Clementine ratios](https://dawngis.dlr.de/data/Vesta/mosaics/HAMO/clementine/Vesta_clementine_HAMO-1-2_global.jp2) — Included from the publisher's original PDS ZIP. The three byte planes preserve the published 26,703 × 13,351 Clementine-style ratio composite. JP2 decoding is unnecessary. Ratios emphasize spectral differences, not mineral abundance.

entries.subject: DLR Dawn HAMO 64 ppd terrain
entries.finding: [DLR Dawn HAMO 64 ppd terrain](https://dawngis.dlr.de/data/Vesta/dtm_vesta.php) — Included. 23,041 × 11,521 big-endian float grid, about 69.5 m spacing. The release page explicitly defines values as radii in meters.

entries.finding: [USGS 48 ppd terrain and relief](https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/search/map/vesta_dawn_fc_hamo_global_dtm_93m) — Excluded in favor of the higher-resolution DLR release and its original coordinate system.

entries.finding: [Le Corre et al. 2017 controlled color mosaics](https://www.hou.usra.edu/meetings/metsoc2017/pdf/6135.pdf) — Unresolved. The conference abstract describes improved registration and planned PDS delivery; this survey has not located a downloadable release corresponding to that work.

entries.finding: [NASA VIR mineral map](https://science.nasa.gov/photojournal/global-mineral-map-of-vesta/) — Excluded: a small explanatory press visualization, not the calibrated global scalar grid needed for a quantitative dataset.

entries.subject: Versioned Vesta test and browser evidence
entries.finding: Lack of dated evidence was the baseline finding. The LAMO update now has focused qualification: three Vesta source/package checks, six projected-image checks and strict preparation types pass. Headless DPR 1/2 checks retain one scene and 800 faces through drag with the same photographic atlas and shadows off. All prior runtime image hashes and draw/hit geometry match the main baseline. New runtime downloads were fetched from their published hash URLs and verified. Evidence is retained beside the body in evidence/lamo-2026-09-14.json; this is not an aggregate build or independent camera-registration result.

entries.subject: DLR Dawn LAMO clear-filter global photographic mosaic
entries.finding: Retrieved the original global 8-bit PNG (80,112 × 40,056) and inspected the companion attached PDS label using a bounded archive range. This is a different observation product from the already selected HAMO color composite and the excluded corrected HAMO grayscale candidate: it retains low-altitude crater and trough photography with source illumination. The label supplies the planetocentric, positive-east Claudia grid, 255 km map radius, 20 m/pixel spacing and fractional pixel offsets. The prepared 8192 × 4096 map and fixed 800-face atlas have coarser display resolution. Exact-black fill is a heuristic because the publisher supplies no independent validity mask; gaps and seams remain visible. Full PDS pixels were not downloaded or compared against the PNG; only the original PNG is the selected photographic input.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a measurement of the observer-camera route
entries.finding: Vesta is the one body with both a survey of deconvolved SPHERE frames and a mapped surface, so its 30 camera-1 frames from 2018 (May 20, June 8 and July 10) are pinned not as a texture source but as a test of the route that photographs Kleopatra, Ausonia, Psyche, Sylvia and Kalliope. Each frame is cast through the shipped HAMO terrain with the camera the route derives from the pinned Dawn pole model (dawn_vesta_v04.tpc: Claudia system, W0 75.39) and pinned Horizons rows at the exposure midpoint, and its correlation with the Dawn colour mosaic is swept over a turn about the pole and over both mirrors. Measured over 30 frames with the limb-fitted centre: the peak sits at +0.5 degrees (median; mean +0.3), 28 of 30 within 3 degrees and all within 5; the model beats the better mirror by 2.5 times (median; 28 of 30 above 1.5). One pixel of disc centre is about one degree of longitude on these 170 to 190 pixel discs, so the residual is at the level of the centre measurement. With the IAU 2015 pole model from pck00011 (W0 285.39) instead, the same frames peak 210 degrees away, the stated distance between the two prime meridians: a kernel in the wrong longitude system is caught here, and by no silhouette. The exposure epoch is the midpoint of the 81 s exposure; using the start moves every peak by 0.75 degrees, which is why the five photographed bodies now state midpoint epochs. No SPHERE dataset is prepared for Vesta: the Dawn mosaics are the surface.

entries.subject: DLR Dawn HAMO-1-2 clear-filter global mosaic (60 m/pixel, May 2013)
entries.finding: The only Dawn product that photographs Vesta's north pole: HAMO-2 (June to July 2012) imaged the northern hemisphere under low northern-spring sun after LAMO and the color HAMO mosaics had left it dark. Measured on the released PNG, the LAMO clear mosaic covers 84 % of the map and none of the band above 75° N; the HAMO-1-2 clear mosaic covers every band, with the 90–75° N band dim (mean 7 of 255) but photographed. It is added as the HAMO photography dataset and as the fallback base of the natural-color and LAMO datasets.

entries.subject: Dawn GRaND hydrogen abundance map (PDS4 dawn-grand-vesta 1.0)
entries.finding: The archived numeric table, not the NASA Vesta Trek colour render, is used: 16,200 two-degree pixels of hydrogen in micrograms per gram (Prettyman et al. 2012), 0.0 to 391.1, no missing pixels and no per-pixel uncertainty. The label says the rows run from -180 E, but the MIN_LON column starts each row at -30 E, so pixels are placed by their own bounds. The catalogue states Claudia Double Prime, 210 degrees from the Claudia frame of the other Vesta maps; packages/bake/authoring/vesta-grand/prepare-grids.mts moves whole pixels by that amount. Checks: the table's column longitudes correlate best with the Trek ColorHydrogen render at zero shift (red channel r = 0.75, swept in 10 degree steps); 4,000 random points read through the shared .npy reader equal a raw-table lookup at Claudia minus 210 degrees; the minimum lies at 303 E, 63 S (Claudia), inside Rheasilvia, as the paper describes. Effective resolution is about 300 km FWHM, far coarser than the 2 degree pixels.

entries.subject: Dawn GRaND corrected iron gamma-ray counting rate map
entries.finding: Included as the archived quantity, a counting rate: 178,698 equal-area pixels, 0.5 degree tall, of 7.6 MeV Fe gamma rays in counts/s corrected for neutron number density (Yamashita et al. 2013), 0.0687 to 0.07746, no missing pixels. Every pixel boundary is a multiple of 0.5 degrees, so the expansion onto 720 x 360 cells is lossless. The catalogue's preliminary factor (Fe wt% = 189.2 x counts/s, scaled to 13.8 wt% mean howardite) is not applied because the catalogue itself advises caution. The uncorrected-counts table is a processing stage of the same measurement and is not added. The grid is one 720 x 360 .npy file; the shared reader finds its range with a loop because a spread of 259,200 values overflows the call stack.

entries.subject: Global geologic map of Vesta, Yingst et al. (2023) linework
entries.finding: A reusable source exists: the ArcGIS layer package on Zenodo (record 19475473, CC BY 4.0, 2026-04-08) holds the polygons of the global map published as Yingst et al. (2023), PSJ 4:157, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acebe9. The shapefile has 136 polygons in 18 hybrid units that combine morphology with Dawn colour classes (for example 'Crater floor material, light blue', symbol cf4), in a 255 km plate carree grid in metres. Its frame is Claudia Double Prime: 19 of 40 Gazetteer craters of 20 to 300 km fall in crater units at zero shift against 9 at the 210 degree Claudia shift. It supersedes the preliminary 2014 map that NASA Vesta Trek shows as a colour render. Not prepared: the existing geology readers take degree shapefiles or GeoTIFFs whose central meridian must equal the recipe's, and none moves a source frame by 210 degrees, so the map cannot be placed on the Claudia mesh without a shared change or a derived re-seamed shapefile. Unit colours live only in the binary .lyr symbology. A second check on 2026-09-27: the .lyr symbology stores each unit colour as three CIE Lab doubles after an RgbColor class id; converting them to sRGB with the D65 or D50 white points, either matrix and either transfer curve leaves up to 0.48 of an 8-bit step, so no conversion reproduces integer author colours and the decoded values cannot be confirmed as the published ones. Third check on 2026-09-27 (ccbf483de8): (a) colours resolved. The layer that draws the shapefile, v106/0005GeoUnits.lyr, symbolizes the 18 SYMBOL codes; converting its stored Lab values with Apple RGB primaries, gamma 1.8 and D65 (packages/telescope-cli/src/source-authoring/esri-symbology.mts) puts all 39 stored colours within 1.0e-6 of integer RGB (plain sRGB: up to 0.498), and the v10 copy is identical. Colour families follow the unit prefixes (crater material yellow-orange, crater floors green, cratered terrain blue, Rheasilvia teal, highlands tan). (b) placement proven. geology-grid.py rasterizes the 136 polygons to 2048 x 1024 with no conflicting pixels; 2,753 cells (0.13%) have no polygon (two south-pole rows, and a column at 30 E Claudia south of 25 S where the source polygons stop at 179.896 E in their frame). Placed at Claudia = source + 210, crater-floor units average 1,120 m below a 10-degree high-pass of the DLR HAMO terrain and crater material 215 m above it; every other 10-degree offset lies between -146 and +217 m for floors, and 208 or 212 degrees give -663 and -546 m. Gazetteer craters 20 to 150 km across fall in crater units 19 of 38 times at that placement against 10 unshifted and a 25% area chance rate; a 2-degree sweep peaks between -10 and +6 degrees. The scientific GeoTIFF reader requires the file's central meridian to equal the recipe's, so geology-grid.py gained a plan field, outputFrame, that writes the Claudia central meridian (-150) while keeping every pixel. Included 2026-09-27: source/geology/prepare-grid.json rasterizes the tracked shapefile with outputFrame; the committed vesta-geologic-units.tif equals the checked grid pixel for pixel and in CRS and transform, and read through the shared reader it again gives 19 of 38 Gazetteer craters in crater units. The source-frame gaps are shown as missing coverage.

entries.subject: Prime meridian of the Gazetteer Vesta feature centres
entries.finding: The Gazetteer centre points use Claudia Double Prime, 210 degrees from the Claudia frame of the maps and mesh; the labels were drawn 210 degrees from their features. With the 210-degree shift all 33 craters 15-80 km across within 40 degrees of the equator sit below the ring one diameter out in the HAMO terrain (median 3.7 km); without it 11 do. The surface map left edge is now 150 E in the Gazetteer frame.

entries.subject: Dawn GRaND fast neutron residual map (PDS4 dawn-grand-vesta 1.0)
entries.finding: Included as archived: 114 quasi-equal-area pixels, 20 degrees tall with 10-degree polar caps, of the residual fast neutron counting rate in counts/s, 1.170 to 1.237, no missing pixels and no per-pixel uncertainty (the catalogue says smoothing over the footprint makes it small). Lawrence et al. (2013) detrended the +Z sensor counts against the epithermal map; the residual follows average atomic mass (about 21.7 amu for diogenite to 23 for basaltic eucrite) and carries an arbitrary offset. Pixel bounds are multiples of 10 degrees in latitude and 1.5 degrees in longitude, so the grid is 240 x 18 cells and lossless. Checks: 4,000 random points through the shared .npy reader equal a raw-table lookup at Claudia minus 210 degrees; the 90-225 E equatorial band the paper calls richest averages 1.221 against a 1.206 global mean with the shift and 1.208 without it; south of 60 S averages 1.195, low as the paper describes for Rheasilvia.

entries.subject: Dawn GRaND high-energy gamma-ray counting rate map
entries.finding: Included as archived: 210 quasi-equal-area pixels, 15 degrees tall with 7.5-degree polar caps, of the corrected high-energy gamma-ray counting rate in counts/s, 12.516 to 13.143, no missing pixels. The catalogue says the rate is corrected for background, solid angle, orientation and cosmic rays, is proportional to heavy major-element content and samples a few tens of decimetres (Peplowski et al. 2013). The archived 1-sigma uncertainty, 0.117 to 0.311 counts/s, and sample counts, 124 to 2,718, are not drawn; the uncertainty is a large share of the range. Grid 360 x 24 cells (7.5 x 1 degree), lossless. Checks: 4,000 random reader points equal the raw table at Claudia minus 210 degrees; the 90-225 E equatorial band averages 12.885 against 12.776 with the shift and 12.815 without; the lowest pixel, 67.5-82.5 S and 270-315 E in Claudia, lies in Rheasilvia.

entries.subject: Dawn GRaND neutron absorption map (DCP)
entries.finding: Included as the archived unitless parameter DCP: 204 quasi-equal-area pixels, 15 degrees tall with 7.5-degree polar caps, -0.0364 to 0.031, no missing pixels, from early-LAMO thermal and epithermal neutrons, 2011-12-08 to 2012-01-14. DCP rises linearly with the macroscopic thermal neutron absorption cross section, which Prettyman et al. (2013) tie to Fe, Ca, Al, Mg and other rock-forming elements and to the eucrite fraction of howardite, at about 300 km resolution. The catalogue's conversion (Sigma = 216.4 x DCP + 66.3, 10^-4 cm2/g) assumes a howardite mean the catalogue calls unknown and is not applied; the 1-sigma uncertainty, 0.0014 to 0.0075, is not drawn. The PDS4 label's modification history names PDS3 DAWN-A-GRAND-5-VESTA-GAMMA-IRON-COR-V1.0 as its source; the PDS3 catalogue gives DAWN-A-GRAND-5-VESTA-ABSORPTION-V1.0, and the table's own columns and checksum match the PDS4 label. Grid 360 x 24 cells, lossless. Checks: 4,000 random reader points equal the raw table at Claudia minus 210 degrees; the 90-225 E equatorial band averages 0.0059 against a -0.0072 mean with the shift and -0.0137 without; south of 60 S averages -0.022, low as the paper reports for Rheasilvia.

entries.subject: Dawn radio-science gravity maps of Vesta: radial gravity, its error, Bouguer anomaly and geoid
entries.finding: The PDS4 bundle urn:nasa:pds:dawn-rss-der-vesta 1.0 (doi:10.17189/av2q-ka20, migrated from PDS3 DAWN-A-RSS-5-VEGR-V2.0, volume DWNVGRS_2) archives gridded maps only for the degree-20 model VESTA20H (Konopliv et al. 2014): ACCEL_0020 (radial gravity without J2 on a 290 x 265 km ellipsoid; the archive says a true anomaly cannot be computed because the series does not converge on the geoid), ACCERR_0020, BOU_0015 (Bouguer to degree 15 only, where the Bouguer spectrum meets the error curve), GEOID_0020 and GEOIDERR_0020 (a = 281.0 km, f = 0.195729537). Each is 181 x 360 little-endian float64 with cell centres at whole degrees from -180 E and 90 N; bytes identical in PDS3 and PDS4. Frame: the field was rotated 210 degrees from the published Claudia frame to near Claudia Double Prime (W0 284.59521, Claudia at 146 E), so the datasets sample the grid at Claudia longitude + 150. Check: the radial gravity correlates with the DLR HAMO radius at r = 0.896 at exactly that shift, against -0.13 unshifted and 0.753 at the best other shift; the geoid peaks at 149 (r = 0.71). Bouguer features against Raymond et al. (2013): maximum 238 mGal inside Vestalia Terra's Gazetteer extent where the Rheasilvia and Veneneia rims approach, +87 over the Rheasilvia centre (91st percentile), +53 over Divalia Fossae (81st); the Veneneia centre reads -1 (48th percentile), not the negative the abstract describes. The geoid is withheld beyond 60 degrees latitude, where the errata say it is not valid (it reaches -2.4e7 m there). Values: radial gravity -1233.6 to 2045.8 mGal, error 19.3 to 169.2, Bouguer -156.4 to 238.2, geoid within 60 degrees -9196.9 to 6912.9 m. Degree 20 is about 42 km at 265 km; Raymond et al. (2013) call the field accurate to about degree 20. No degree-strength map is archived. The pds3-grid reader needs the detached-pointer and latitude-limit additions drafted with this change.

entries.subject: VESTA26J degree-26 gravity model (Park et al. 2025)
entries.finding: The same bundle archives VESTA26J as coefficients only (data-shadr and data-shbdr), with no gridded map; showing it would need our own summation, which this package does not do.
entries.revisitWhen: A gridded VESTA26J product is archived, or a shared coefficient-synthesis capability is approved.

entries.subject: VESTA20H geoid error map (JGDWN_VES20H_GEOIDERR_0020)
entries.finding: Archived and decoded (40.5 to 88.9 m, one sigma) but not shown: the same errata limit it to about 60 degrees of latitude, and the radial gravity error dataset already shows where the model is weak.
entries.revisitWhen: Readers ask how far the geoid itself may be off.
